pl-l4d6c3-d1e115.summary: Notes that though one is immersed three times for the mystery of the Trinity, it counts as one baptism.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e121.summary: States that no one can be baptized in the mother's womb, even if the mother is baptized.
claims: Baptism of the mother does not baptize the child in the womb.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e124.summary: Quotes Isidore: those in the womb cannot be baptized, since one not yet born according to Adam cannot be reborn according to Christ, and regeneration cannot be said of one in whom generation has not preceded.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e131.summary: Adds Augustine: no one can be reborn before he is born.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e140.summary: Answers the objection from Jeremiah and John the Baptist, said to be sanctified from the womb, as some think also of Jacob: if inner cleansing is meant, it must be counted among the miracles of divine power, as Augustine says hesitantly: if the use of reason and will was so accelerated in that child that he could know and believe in the womb, it is a miracle of divine power, not a pattern of human nature, as God once made a beast speak.
claims: Sanctification in the womb, if real cleansing, is a miracle, not a natural pattern.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e149.summary: Adds Augustine: of Jeremiah it is written 'before you came from the womb I sanctified you', but the sanctification by which we become God's temple belongs only to the reborn, and no one is reborn unless first born; so that sanctification can be taken as predestination.
claims: Jeremiah's sanctification may be taken as predestination.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e161.summary: Notes that Augustine seems to speak hesitantly, since he also says that it is not said the infant believed in the womb but that he leapt; Elizabeth did not say he leapt in faith but in her womb; the sanctification may have been a sign of so great a thing, to be recognized by an adult, not known by the child.
claims: Augustine hesitates whether John's leap was faith or a sign.

pl-l4d6c3-d1e167.summary: Concludes that Augustine speaks without assertion, not deciding whether the sanctification was a sign of something future or true justification by the Spirit. Lombard holds it better to say that they were justified in the womb beyond the common law and anticipated by grace, all their sins forgiven, as many saints attest.
claims: Jeremiah and John were justified in the womb beyond the common law.

pl-l4d6c3.summary: Notes that though one is immersed three times for the Trinity, it counts as one baptism. No one can be baptized in the mother's womb, even if the mother is baptized, since one not yet born according to Adam cannot be reborn according to Christ, as Isidore and Augustine say. As for Jeremiah and John the Baptist, said to be sanctified from the womb, Augustine speaks hesitantly: if inner cleansing is meant, it is a miracle of divine power, not a pattern of nature; the sanctification may be taken as predestination, or as a sign recognized by others. Lombard holds it better to say they were justified in the womb beyond the common law and freed from all sins, as many saints attest.
claims: No one can be baptized in the womb, since rebirth requires birth.
Augustine speaks hesitantly about sanctification in the womb.
Lombard holds that Jeremiah and John were justified in the womb beyond the common law.
